strings.name: Guido Imbens
strings.summary: Imbens studies identification of causal relationships in non-randomized data. With Joshua Angrist he developed instrumental-variable and local-average-treatment-effect frameworks, helping connect econometrics and statistics. He taught at Harvard, Berkeley and Stanford and shared the 2021 economics prize with Angrist and David Card. These methods depend on explicit assumptions; correlation does not automatically establish causation.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; reviewed on 15 November. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Developed statistical methods for causal inference, allowing observational data to be used more reliably in policy evaluation.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education

strings.highlights.h1.title: Causal identification
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Angrist developed local average treatment effects, clarifying whose effects instrumental-variable methods identify.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Connecting disciplines
strings.highlights.h2.text: Advanced potential-outcome, matching and policy-evaluation methods across econometrics and statistics.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Shared economics prize
strings.timeline.t1.text: Shared the methodological half of the prize with Angrist; Card received the other half.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Co-authored causal-inference book
strings.timeline.t2.text: Co-authored Causal Inference for Statistics, Social, and Biomedical Sciences with Donald Rubin.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Joined Stanford
strings.timeline.t3.text: Joined Stanford Graduate School of Business.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Began teaching at Berkeley
strings.timeline.t4.text: Began teaching at UC Berkeley before later returning to Harvard.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Published potential-outcomes framework
strings.timeline.t5.text: Published with Angrist and Rubin, placing instrumental variables within a potential-outcomes framework.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Developed LATE method
strings.timeline.t6.text: Published the local-average-treatment-effect paper with Angrist.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Earned Brown economics PhD
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned an economics PhD at Brown, having already begun teaching at Harvard.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed Hull master’s training
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed master’s training in economics and econometrics at Hull.
